Face ID for Home Assistant

Names on your camera notifications, from the faces you already tagged in Immich. Detection and matching run on your own machine: no cloud service, no subscription, no face data leaving your network.

InsightFace buffalo_lImmich + pgvector Home AssistantFastAPIPython

From motion to a name

Every motion frame your cameras save is checked automatically, usually within a second on an ordinary CPU.

MotionA camera detects movement and Home Assistant saves a frame.
Face ID serviceInsightFace finds each face and turns it into a 512-number fingerprint.
Match in ImmichThe fingerprint is compared with the people you named in your photo library.
Annotated copyA faces- image with names drawn on it is saved next to the original.
Home AssistantYour notification says who was seen; automations can react to it.

The review report

A report lists every image with numbered boxes (green = identified, red = unidentified), a crop of each face, the distance, and the next-best candidate. Below, the same frame is run at two thresholds: the normal one (0.42) identifies the person; a stricter one (0.30) refuses to guess and shows the face as unidentified, with the closest candidate for review. A lower threshold means fewer false matches and more “Unknown”.

Why it is reliable

  • Uses Immich’s own face model, so embeddings are directly comparable.
  • Matches only people you named; unnamed clusters cannot cause a wrong name.
  • Re-detects the Immich database schema automatically after upgrades.
  • Failures never break your automation: it falls back to the original image.
  • On 400 faces from my own library, the default threshold gave about 98.7% precision (an optimistic test, because neighbours often come from the same photo burst).

Built for a smart home

  • Works with any Home Assistant camera, including Blink.
  • Events and sensors in Home Assistant; optional MQTT auto-discovery.
  • API-key protected, input-validated, and tested (100+ automated tests).
  • Daily read-only health check that an AI agent can run and explain.
  • Annotated copies follow your existing retention rules.

Private by default

  • Everything runs on your hardware; nothing is sent to a cloud.
  • Only the faces you tagged in Immich are known.
  • Images are kept only as long as your own retention job keeps them.
  • Not a security or access-control system: no liveness or anti-spoofing checks.
